finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::raw_text_oids only covers scalar date/timestamp/timestamptz; array and range date/time types still get parsed into js `date` and remain timezone-shifted
evidence: In packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts:20-36, RAW_TEXT_OIDS contains only the three scalar OIDs (DATE 1082, TIMESTAMP 1114, TIMESTAMPTZ 1184) and datasourceTypeParser delegates every other OID to pg-types' default parser. pg-types' textParsers registers parseDateArray for 1115 (timestamp[]), 1182 (date[]) and 1185 (timestamptz[]), which builds JS Date objects per element via the same local-time parse the comment says is wrong, so array-typed date/timestamp columns still come back as Dates and toCell/JSON.stringify emits ISO strings shifted by the Node runtime offset for `timestamp`/`date` arrays — the claim's core point holds. The claim is partly inaccurate about range types: pg-types does not register parsers for 3908/3910/3912 (only 3907 numrange[] as strings), so tsrange/tstzrange/daterange already fall through as raw text; that detail is wrong but incidental to the finding. I verified the service file directly; the pg-types parser table is from knowledge of the library rather than the pinned source, hence medium confidence.
